name: Oded
overview: Oded is a male figure mentioned in the Bible primarily as the father of Azariah. The Scripture does not specify his tribe or provide additional personal details beyond his paternal role. His identification is concise, focusing on his relationship to his son within the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Oded means "restorer," which is a proper name recorded in 2 Chronicles 15:1. This meaning reflects a theme of renewal or restoration, though the name itself was not given by God according to the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Oded as the father of Azariah, as noted in 2 Chronicles 15:1. Beyond this paternal relationship, no further family connections or relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Oded's significance in Scripture is primarily tied to his role as the father of Azariah, a prophetic figure who appears in 2 Chronicles 15. While Oded himself does not have a direct narrative role, his mention establishes the lineage of Azariah, linking him to the broader story of restoration and encouragement found in the passage.
